data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is a performative contradiction in Popper's system: it is defensible only as an irrational 'leap of faith' that Popper rhetorically disguises as rational methodology, costing the coherence of his critical rationalism.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If Popper admits the 'leap of faith' openly without calling it 'rational,' the contradiction dissolves into honest existentialism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'methodological rule' is accepted as a definition of rationality itself (stipulative), the contradiction vanishes but the term 'rational' loses its normative force.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Performative Contradiction Analysis: Arguing that the injunction to 'prefer the best tested' functions as a dogma within a system designed to eliminate dogmas, revealing a foundational gap filled by rhetoric rather than logic.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
